title: The Angel did not have to tap
story: My Hypnotic Specter was still tapped from my last attack when my opponent declared Serra Angel and Kird Ape as attackers. Their Taiga kept the Ape at 2/3. I was at six life, with an untapped Maze of Ith and no available blocker. The Angel had vigilance, so it had not tapped to attack, but I tapped Maze targeting it anyway. The Angel stayed attacking, unable to deal combat damage this turn. The Ape still connected for two. I moved my life total to four, leaving Maze tapped beside my Swamp .
era: 2015 Old School 93/94 using modern combat rules
matchup: Mono Black against multicolor creature midrange

review.basis: Mark Arce's published 2015 Old School Mono-Black deck includes Maze, Hypnotic Specter and Swamp; opposing creature package is a fictional multicolor matchup, not his documented opponent. An earlier-turn attack can leave Specter tapped during the opponent's turn. Serra Angel attacks untapped because of vigilance yet is a legal target for Maze, which does not remove it from combat. Taiga's Forest land type makes Kird Ape 2/3. One Maze activation costs tapping it and zero mana. A second unblocked attacker still deals 2, changing 6 life to 4.
review.scenario: representative reconstruction; not a recorded match, quotation, or claimed opponent registration

manualReview: Hypnotic Specter can stay tapped on opponent's turn after attacking previously. Opposing Serra Angel has vigilance and can attack without tapping; Maze may target it anyway. Taiga is a Forest and grants Kird Ape +1/+2, making it 2/3. The unblocked Ape deals 2 while the prevented Angel deals 0; life 6→4. Maze activation taps and spends zero mana. 2015 modern combat rules explicit.
